qc.label_under_test: the operator or gap just before an item is repeated (squaring '5 cm * 5 cm', a doubled block '0110 0110', 'outer(o, o)'): the model expects the next item to copy the previous one, as against the same layout where the next item differs
qc.notes: Picked for its link to the echoes map (copying). Probes of idiomatic doubling, where the next item really is a copy, read 0.01-0.02 (bye bye, New York, New York, knock, knock, mayday, mayday, very very) and '1 1 2 2 3 3' only 0.11, so 'the model expects the next item to copy the previous one' is too broad: the old test's fire items all announced the repeat. This refine names the announcement. I read this pole's earlier test before writing mine (the brief asks to read it after drafting): none of its sentences or frames are reused, and these 16 sentences were scored 0 times before this commit.

neighbours.label: the operator or gap just before an item is repeated, when the text ANNOUNCES or computes the repeat (twice, doubled, two times, side x side of a square, a cube); idiomatic reduplications that copy without announcing it (bye bye, knock knock, New York, New York, tick tock) stay quiet, as does an announced join of two different items
fire: Saying the word ping twice gives ping ping on the screen.
If we double the string xy we get xy xy in the log.

quiet: As we left, the toddler said bye bye from the porch.
Every knock knock joke ends in a pun.
